subject: Re: Pilot feedback: Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha) — install findings + doc clarifications
body:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@heliobank.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@heliobank.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@heliobank.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 8:14 AM PST
Subject: Pilot feedback: Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha) — install findings + doc clarifications
Attachments: HelioBank-RedwoodPrivate-NetworkDiagram-v2.pdf

Markus,

Thanks again for the support yesterday. We got through the Terraform apply + installer run, but wanted to capture findings while it’s fresh.

High-level: we’re aligned on the overall pattern (private-only VPC, no IGW, endpoints everywhere), but the “happy path” example reads like NAT is assumed in a few places.

What worked
- Baseline VPC + subnet tiering came up cleanly (no CIDR overlap issues).
- VPC endpoints for ECR and CloudWatch Logs resolved most of the “can’t pull / can’t emit logs” problems once created.
- Installer preflight checks were helpful (but a few error messages didn’t give us the exact endpoint to add).

What blocked / required changes
1) STS endpoint (interface) was needed even in our “no public egress” setup.
   - Without it, installer failed during auth/bootstrap (we didn’t expect STS to be required for image pulls).

2) S3 gateway endpoint route table association
   - We initially associated the S3 gateway endpoint only to the “private” route tables; our isolated subnets couldn’t reach S3 until we also associated it there.

3) DNS / private DNS expectation
   - We had private DNS disabled on ECR endpoints initially because our internal DNS team wanted explicit approvals.
   - Without private DNS, the installer couldn’t resolve the ECR hostname in a way that was obvious to troubleshoot.
   - Suggestion: docs should explicitly say “private DNS on endpoints = required unless you provide equivalent resolver rules + DNS overrides,” and spell out what “equivalent” means.

4) NAT language in docs
   - We do not have NAT in this environment; egress is via an internal proxy / centralized egress VPC.
   - The quickstart reads as if NAT is “optional” but a few troubleshooting sections imply it’s required.

Requested doc clarifications
- Exact list of REQUIRED interface endpoints for the installer path (ECR api, ECR dkr, CloudWatch Logs, STS, …anything else?)
- For S3: confirm gateway endpoint required + which route tables must be associated (private + isolated)
- “No public egress” recipe: a complete example tfvars + callouts about DNS and endpoint policies
- If you expect Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints in the customer account (or not)

We attached an updated network diagram showing our actual topology and where we placed endpoints.

Attachment:
- HelioBank-RedwoodPrivate-NetworkDiagram-v2.pdf (VPC + subnet tiers + route tables + endpoints)

Happy to jump on a quick call today if helpful.

Raj Patel
Network Engineering
HelioBank

Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 9:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Pilot feedback: Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha) — install findings + doc clarifications

Raj — super helpful, thank you. We’ve been trying to flush out exactly these “locked-down enterprise” gaps before we call the modules usable outside PS.

A few quick notes / questions so we can turn this into doc + module improvements:

- STS: yes, we’ve seen this come up (installer bootstrap + some AWS SDK calls in our control-plane components). Ethan can confirm whether STS is hard-required for all Private installs or only specific modes.
- S3 gateway association: agree this should be explicitly stated. We’ll update the quickstart to call out “associate to ALL subnets used by workloads that need S3 access (including isolated).”
- Private DNS on endpoints: agree we need a clearer stance. Our default should be “private DNS on” for the required endpoints, and if a customer can’t enable it, we should list the alternate DNS approach + what breaks.

Can you confirm which subnets you ran the installer components from (private vs isolated), and whether you were using an existing corporate DNS resolver (on-prem) vs Route53 Resolver endpoints inside the VPC?

We can set up 30 min today. Colin will send a calendar hold.

Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@heliobank.com>
Cc: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@heliobank.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@heliobank.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Colin O'Donnell <colin.odonnell@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 10:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Pilot feedback: Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha) — install findings + doc clarifications

Adding a couple of infra-specific clarifications we can bake into the alpha defaults.

1) NAT / “no public egress” stance
- Our module should not imply NAT is required. For Private deployments, NAT is only one of several valid egress models (NAT, centralized egress/proxy, or fully private w/ endpoints only).
- For HelioBank’s pattern (centralized egress): the recommended config is to disable IGW + disable NAT creation and ensure endpoints cover all AWS services needed.

2) S3 gateway endpoint association
- Agree with Raj’s point: the S3 gateway endpoint must be associated with every route table whose subnets need S3 access.
- We can make this safer by having the endpoints module accept a list of route table IDs and default to “private + isolated route tables” when using our baseline module.

3) Private DNS on interface endpoints
- If private DNS is off, customers need to manage DNS resolution for service names (e.g., *.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com). That’s a non-trivial “you own it” path.
- I recommend docs treat it as REQUIRED for the alpha quickstart, with an “advanced” appendix for private-DNS-off environments.

Raj — if you can share whether your internal DNS is forwarding to VPC Resolver (typical) vs you require explicit Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints, that will help us write the right guidance.

Irene Choi
Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Pilot feedback: Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha) — install findings + doc clarifications

Thanks Raj — I’m going to translate this into doc deltas today.

Proposed doc updates (draft outline)
1) “Required endpoints” table
- Required (alpha): ECR (api + dkr), S3 (gateway), CloudWatch Logs, STS
- Optional: SSM (only if using it for ops workflows), KMS (if customer policies require explicit endpoint), etc.

2) S3 gateway: explicit route table checklist
- “Associate S3 gateway endpoint with private + isolated RTs (or any RT used by installer/runtime nodes).”

3) Private DNS expectations
- Call out: “For alpha quickstart we require private DNS enabled on interface endpoints.”
- Add an appendix: “Private DNS disabled: what you must configure (DNS forwarders, conditional rules, validation commands).”

4) “No public egress” example
- Add a complete tfvars snippet + a validation section (dig/curl to endpoints, test ECR auth, etc.)

Raj/Sarah: if you can answer one question, it will help a lot — do you require endpoint policies on ECR/S3 (deny-by-default with specific principals), or is security comfortable with default endpoint policies + SG restrictions?

Kira Thompson
Technical Writing (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot feedback: Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha) — install findings + doc clarifications
Attachments: installer-preflight-failure-sts-endpoint.png

All — a few security questions from our side.

1) STS endpoint
- Can you confirm it’s required (and why) for the Private deployment? We need it called out explicitly in the security review.
- Attaching a screenshot of the preflight error we saw prior to adding STS.

Attachment:
- installer-preflight-failure-sts-endpoint.png

2) Endpoint policies
- We prefer explicit endpoint policies on S3 and (if possible) on ECR. If you have recommended policy templates, that would be ideal.

3) Logging / retention
- We enabled VPC flow logs to CloudWatch in our test account.
- What’s Redwood’s recommended retention (we typically do 365 days in regulated environments)?
- Any requirement from Redwood that logs be accessible to Redwood support during incidents (we prefer customer-only access)?

If you can answer (3) in writing, I can close out this section of our risk register for the pilot.

Sarah Kim
Security Architecture
HelioBank

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@heliobank.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@heliobank.com>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@heliobank.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Kira Thompson <kira.thompson@redwoodinference.com>, Colin O'Donnell <colin.odonnell@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 4:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Pilot feedback: Redwood Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha) — install findings + doc clarifications

Sarah — got it.

1) STS endpoint
Ethan confirmed: for the current alpha installer path, STS is treated as REQUIRED when running fully private (no public egress). It’s used by AWS SDK calls during bootstrap/auth and a couple of preflight validations. We’re updating the docs and installer error text to name STS explicitly (instead of a generic “AWS auth failed”).

2) Endpoint policies
We don’t have “one size fits all” templates yet (because customers vary on principal scoping), but we can provide recommended starting points:
- S3 gateway endpoint policy: restrict to the specific buckets/prefixes used for artifacts and block all other buckets.
- ECR interface endpoint policy: allow only the needed ECR actions for pull (GetAuthorizationToken, BatchGetImage, GetDownloadUrlForLayer, etc.) scoped to your account/approved repos.
Irene/Kira will follow up with a doc appendix + example snippets.

3) Logging / retention + Redwood access
- Retention: Redwood does not require a specific retention period; we typically recommend 30–90 days as a baseline for operability, and longer (e.g., 365 days) if your compliance requires it.
- Access: we do not require direct access to your logs. In incident workflows, customers usually share relevant excerpts/exports or grant time-bound access if their policies allow. The modules should keep log ownership/customer control by default.

Next steps / action items (we’ll track on our side)
- [Docs] Add REQUIRED endpoints table and explicitly call out STS requirement for private-only mode.
- [Docs] Add “no public egress” tfvars example + validation checklist.
- [Modules] Make S3 gateway association safer by defaulting to private+isolated route tables when using vpc-baseline.
- [Installer] Improve preflight error strings to name missing endpoints (ECR api vs dkr, STS, etc.).

Colin sent a hold for Monday to walk through any remaining items.

Markus Klein
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
